WITH trans_avgs AS (
  SELECT transref, AVG(anlycount) as trans_avg
  FROM sentimentandfundamentals
  WHERE anlycount IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY transref
),
overall_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(trans_avg) as overall_avg
  FROM trans_avgs
),
kept_transactions AS (
  SELECT ta.transref, ta.trans_avg
  FROM trans_avgs ta
  CROSS JOIN overall_avg oa
  WHERE ta.trans_avg > oa.overall_avg
),
kept_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(trans_avg) as kept_avg
  FROM kept_transactions
),
results_with_rank AS (
  SELECT 
    kt.transref,
    kt.trans_avg,
    kt.trans_avg - oa.overall_avg as above_overall,
    kt.trans_avg - ka.kept_avg as above_kept,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY kt.trans_avg - ka.kept_avg DESC NULLS LAST) as rn
  FROM kept_transactions kt
  CROSS JOIN overall_avg oa
  CROSS JOIN kept_avg ka
)
SELECT transref, trans_avg, above_overall, above_kept
FROM results_with_rank
WHERE rn <= 10 OR above_kept IS NOT DISTINCT FROM (SELECT above_kept FROM results_with_rank WHERE rn = 10)
ORDER BY above_kept DESC NULLS LAST;

assumptions.assumption: Row position (not rank with ties) determines "the 10th": the query uses ROW_NUMBER to identify the 10th sorted row by position, then includes all rows matching its above_kept value. If ties should be handled by rank (all rows with the 10th-highest distinct value), use DENSE_RANK instead.

alternatives.interpretation: "The 10th" refers to the 10th distinct value (rank), not position. Include all rows with rank ≤ 10 using DENSE_RANK, so all rows with the same above_kept value as the lowest-ranked included row are returned together.
